250	/-! ## §3. Cluster-P consequences that no longer need the ledger
251	
252	The two statements cluster P actually wants downstream are a **section lower bound**
253	(Riemann inequality) and an **H¹ vanishing criterion**.  Both follow from the ungated χ
254	formula without `hledger`, `hbump`, or any exactness hypothesis.  What they still need is
255	the *geometric* input relating the chart dimensions to `deg D`; that input is isolated as
256	an explicit hypothesis rather than hidden, and it is the honest residual leaf. -/
257	
258	/-- **Riemann inequality, gate-free.**  `ℓ(D) ≥ χ(D)` is elementary (`chi_le_ell`), so the
259	ungated χ formula turns any lower bound on the Čech count into a lower bound on `ℓ(D)`:
260	
261	`dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D) ≤ ℓ(D)`.
262	
263	Compare `SectionBounds.degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell` and
264	`BoundedVanishing.exists_bound_ell_eq`, which reach comparable conclusions only under
265	`hledger`.  Here there is no ledger hypothesis at all; the content has moved into the
266	computable left-hand side. -/
267	theorem charts_sub_overlap_le_ell (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
268	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
269	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
270	    (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
271	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
272	      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) := by
273	  rw [← chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
274	  exact chi_le_ell k U₀ U₁ D
275	
276	/-- **H¹ vanishing is equivalent to the Čech count being exact** — no gate.
277	
278	`Ȟ¹(D) = 0` iff `dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D) = ℓ(D)`, i.e. iff the
279	inclusion–exclusion count computes `ℓ(D)` on the nose.
280	
281	This is the vanishing criterion cluster P needs, and unlike
282	`BoundedVanishing.subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` (a restatement of `𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`) it is a
283	**numerical** criterion: it can be certified by counting dimensions on the two charts,
284	which is what an explicit cover computation actually produces.  Note it is a genuine
285	two-way reduction, not a reformulation of `h1dim = 0` — the right-hand side mentions only
286	the three chart dimensions and `ℓ`. -/
287	theorem h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
288	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
289	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
290	    h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 ↔
291	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
292	        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
293	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ) := by
294	  have h := chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D
295	  rw [chi] at h
296	  omega
297	
298	/-- **Uniform vanishing from a uniform chart count.**  If above some weighted-degree
299	threshold `b` the Čech count is exact at every divisor, then `h¹` vanishes uniformly above
300	`b`.  The quantifier structure is the one cluster P's consumers take, and the hypothesis is
301	now a statement about chart dimensions rather than about a connecting homomorphism.
302	
303	This is deliberately stated with the finiteness binders as an instance-quantified
304	hypothesis, matching `ResidueField.UniformlyBoundedVanishing`'s shape, so that a consumer
305	proving the chart count over a family of divisors gets uniform vanishing directly. -/
306	theorem exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero_of_charts (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (b : ℤ)
307	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
308	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
309	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
310	    (hcount : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
311	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
312	        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
313	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ)) :
314	    ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D → h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 :=
315	  fun D hD => (h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts k U₀ U₁ hcov D).mpr (hcount D hD)
316	
317	end ChiCharts

319	/-! ## §4. The principal-divisor leaf, with the ledger removed from the hypothesis list
320	
321	`SectionBounds.degK_principal_eq_zero` derives `deg_k(div g) = 0` from the **closed ledger**.
322	But the ingredient it really uses is `ClassInvariance.chi_eq_of_principal_shift`
323	(`χ(D − div g) = χ(D)`), which is already *unconditional* in this lane — the ledger enters
324	only to convert a χ-equality into a degree-equality.
325	
326	So the ledger can be replaced by the ungated χ formula, and what remains is visibly the
327	**one honest geometric input**: that the Čech chart count sees `deg_k`.  Stating it that way
328	turns the open leaf `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` from "needs the ledger"
329	(a global hypothesis over all divisors, refutable-looking, hard to certify) into "needs the
330	chart count at two divisors", which an explicit cover computation can supply. -/
331	
332	section PrincipalLeaf
333	
334	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
335	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
336	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
337	
338	/-- **The Čech count is `deg_k` up to the constant `χ(0)`** — the single geometric input.
339	
340	`ChartCountsDegree` says the unconditional Čech Euler characteristic
341	(`chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap`) is an affine function of the weighted degree with slope one.
342	Given the ungated formula, this is *equivalent* to the closed ledger `hledger`, but it is
343	stated in terms of the three chart dimensions, which is what makes it checkable on an
344	explicit cover — and it is honest that this, and not any exactness datum, is the content.
345	
346	This is deliberately a `def` of a Prop rather than a class: the lane's instance-diamond
347	hazard (recorded in `ResidueField.lean`) makes a new global class a liability here. -/
348	def ChartCountsDegree : Prop :=
349	  ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D
350	
351	/-- **Principal divisors have weighted degree zero, from χ class-invariance alone.**
352	
353	Identical conclusion to `SectionBounds.degK_principal_eq_zero`; the point is the proof's
354	shape.  The only two facts used are `ClassInvariance.chi_eq_of_principal_shift` (which is
355	unconditional in this lane) and the chart count at the two divisors `0` and `0 − div g`.
356	No exactness hypothesis, no `hbump`, no approximation input. -/
357	theorem degK_principal_eq_zero_of_chartCounts
358	    (hcount : ChartCountsDegree k U₀ U₁) {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
359	    degK k (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by
360	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_principal_shift k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor) hg
361	  rw [hcount ((0 : X.WeilDivisor) - Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg),
362	    hcount (0 : X.WeilDivisor), degK_sub, degK_zero] at hchi
363	  omega
364	
365	/-- **The chart count is EQUIVALENT to the closed ledger.**
366	
367	Both directions are immediate from `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap`, since `ChartCountsDegree` is
368	by definition the ledger.  This lemma is recorded for exactly one reason: to make it
369	impossible for a later reader to mistake `ChartCountsDegree` for a *weakening* of the
370	ledger.  It is not a reduction — it is a restatement in checkable terms, and inbox memory
371	`I-0456` records that presenting a restatement as a reduction is this task's recurring
372	failure mode.  The honest gain is not logical strength; it is that the right-hand side is
373	computable on a cover, whereas `hbump` invited a search for a connecting homomorphism that
374	this lane never had. -/
375	theorem chartCountsDegree_iff_ledger :
376	    ChartCountsDegree k U₀ U₁ ↔
377	      ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D :=
378	  Iff.rfl
379	
380	end PrincipalLeaf
381	
382	end Adelic
383	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# The Čech Euler characteristic is an inclusion–exclusion count — unconditionally
10	
11	Every χ-statement in this lane so far has been *gated*: `ChiLedger.chi_add` and its
12	descendants take four exactness hypotheses (`window`, `connect`, `twist`, and the
13	surjectivity `htwist`) packaging the ledger four-term sequence
14	`0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0`, whose connecting map and
15	right-exactness the lane does not construct.  That is why `hbump` — "χ jumps by
16	`[κ(P):k]` at every one-point bump" — has been carried as an open hypothesis, and why
17	the audit at inbox `I-0449` was able to *refute* it off the cover overlap.
18	
19	This file removes the gate for the underlying numerical identity.  The point is that
20	for a **two-set cover** the Čech Euler characteristic needs no exact sequence at all:
21	
22	`χ(D) = dim 𝒞⁰(D) − dim 𝒞¹(D)` where `𝒞⁰(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊕ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))`,
23	`𝒞¹(D) = 𝒜(D) = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁, 𝒪(D))`,
24	
25	and both `ℓ(D) = dim ker` and `h¹(D) = dim coker` are read off the *same* map by
26	rank–nullity.  Concretely, with `B(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the coboundary and
27	`L(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the global sections (`Substrate.linearSystem_eq_inf`
28	on a cover), the modular law
29	`dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) = dim S₀ + dim S₁`
30	(mathlib's `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`) *is* the Euler characteristic:
31	
32	`χ(D) = ℓ(D) − h¹(D) = dim L(D) − (dim 𝒜(D) − dim B(D))`
33	      `= dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D) = dim S₀ + dim S₁ − dim 𝒜(D)`.
34	
35	## What is proved, and what it is worth
36	
37	* `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — **the unconditional χ formula.**
38	  `χ(D) = dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D)` on a cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
39	  with **no exactness hypotheses** — only the finiteness of the two chart section
40	  spaces.  This is strictly stronger than what `chi_add` gives, in the precise sense
41	  that it has none of `chi_add`'s four gated binders.
42	
43	* `chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — the difference form: the χ-jump between two
44	  divisors is an alternating sum of three *local step* dimensions, again unconditionally.
45	
46	* `chi_add_of_charts` — **gate-free χ-additivity.**  `χ(D') = χ(D) + (local overlap step)`
47	  precisely when the two chart steps vanish.  Compare `ChiLedger.chi_add`, which reaches
48	  the same conclusion from four exactness hypotheses: this version replaces all four by a
49	  *checkable* condition on the two charts.
50	
51	* `chi_add_eq_residueDeg_of_charts` — the one-point bump with the residue degree, from
52	  the chart condition plus strong approximation (`hsurj`), no exactness gate.
53	
54	* `chi_add_of_notMem_overlap` — **`χ` is constant across an off-overlap bump, and this
55	  is now a THEOREM, not a refutation of a hypothesis.**  Where `I-0449`'s
56	  `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` derived a contradiction *from* `chi_add`'s hypotheses
57	  (a conditional refutation), this proves `χ(1·P + E) = χ(E)` outright.  Consequently:
58	
59	* `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap_unconditional` — `hbump` is **unconditionally false** at
60	  every off-overlap prime, on every curve with a nonempty off-overlap prime and finite
61	  chart sections.  This is the sharp form the audit at `I-0456` asked for ("WHERE is H
62	  false?") and it settles the status of `hbump`: it is not merely unproved off the
63	  overlap, it is refutable there, so `chi_eq_of_bump` must not be advertised as the
64	  ledger's route.  See §4 for what survives.
65	
66	## Provenance
67	
68	Rederived in AJC's own abstractions (`sectionSub`, `chi`, `H1Mod`).  This is **not** a
69	port: the sibling project's `RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` core is a bounded
70	vanishing statement, not this identity, and nothing of this shape existed in either
71	project — the lane had only the gated `chi_add`.  The mathlib input is exactly one
72	lemma, `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`.
73	-/
74	
75	set_option autoImplicit false
76	
77	universe u
78	
79	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
80	open scoped WithZero
81	
82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
83	namespace Adelic
84	
85	section ChiCharts
86	
87	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
88	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
89	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
90	
91	/-- **`L(D)` is the intersection of the two chart section spaces**, as `k`-submodules.
92	The `k`-linear form of `Substrate.linearSystem_eq_inf`. -/
93	theorem sectionSub_top_eq_inf (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
94	    sectionSub k ⊤ D = sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D := by
95	  apply SetLike.coe_injective
96	  show (sectionOfDivisor ⊤ D : Set X.functionField) = _
97	  rw [show sectionOfDivisor (X := X) ⊤ D = linearSystem D from rfl,
98	    linearSystem_eq_inf hcov D]
99	  rfl
100	
101	/-- **The unconditional Čech Euler characteristic.**  On a two-set cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
102	
103	`χ(D) = dim_k Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim_k Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim_k 𝒜(D)`.
104	
105	**No exactness hypotheses.**  The only inputs are the cover and the finiteness of the two
106	chart section spaces; `𝒜(D)`'s finiteness follows, since `𝒜(D) ⊇ B(D)` is not needed —
107	what is needed is that `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is finite-dimensional, which is the binder
108	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)`.
109	
110	Proof: `ℓ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁)` (the cover, `sectionSub_top_eq_inf`) and
111	`h¹(D) = dim 𝒜(D) − dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁)` (rank–nullity for the quotient `𝒜(D)/B(D)`), so
112	`χ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D)`, and the modular law
113	`Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq` replaces the first two terms by
114	`dim S₀ + dim S₁`. -/
115	theorem chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
116	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
117	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
118	    chi k U₀ U₁ D = (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
119	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
120	      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) := by
121	  classical
122	  -- `h¹(D) + dim B(D) = dim 𝒜(D)`: rank–nullity for `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D) / B(D)`.
123	  have hcob : Module.finrank k (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)
124	      + Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
125	          (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
126	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) :=
127	    Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank _
128	  -- The comap of `B(D)` into `𝒜(D)` has the same dimension as `B(D)` itself,
129	  -- because `B(D) ≤ 𝒜(D)`.
130	  have hBeq : Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
131	      (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)) = Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D) :=
132	    (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe (coboundarySub_le_overlap k U₀ U₁ D)).finrank_eq
133	  -- The modular law for the two chart subspaces.
134	  have hmod : Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)
135	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField)
136	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D) :=
137	    Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq _ _
138	  -- `ℓ(D) = dim (S₀ ⊓ S₁)` by the cover.
139	  have hell : ell k D
140	      = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField) := by
141	    rw [ell, sectionSub_top_eq_inf k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
142	  rw [hBeq] at hcob
143	  simp only [chi, h1dim, hell]
144	  omega
145	
146	/-- **The unconditional χ-difference formula.**  The χ-jump between any two divisors is
147	the alternating sum of the two chart steps and the overlap step:
148	
149	`χ(D') − χ(D) = ΔS₀ + ΔS₁ − Δ𝒜`
150	
151	where each `Δ` is the difference of the corresponding dimensions.  Again no exactness
152	hypotheses.  This is the honest replacement for `ChiLedger.chi_add`. -/
153	theorem chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D D' : X.WeilDivisor)
154	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
155	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
156	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D')] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D')]
157	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D')] :
158	    chi k U₀ U₁ D' - chi k U₀ U₁ D =
159	      ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D') : ℤ) - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D))
160	      + ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D') : ℤ) - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D))
161	      - ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D') : ℤ)
162	          - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)) := by
163	  rw [chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D, chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D']
164	  ring
165	
166	/-- **A one-point bump does not change the sections over an open missing that point.**
167	`Γ(U, 𝒪(1·P + E)) = Γ(U, 𝒪(E))` when `P.point ∉ U`, because `Γ(U, −)` reads the divisor
168	only at primes meeting `U`.
169	
170	This is `LedgerClosure.sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap` with the overlap
171	`U₀ ⊓ U₁` generalised to an arbitrary open — the generalisation is what lets the same
172	computation be run at *all three* terms of the Čech count below. -/
173	theorem sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem (U : X.Opens)
174	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
175	    sectionSub k U (pointDivisor P + E) = sectionSub k U E := by
176	  apply le_antisymm
177	  · intro x hx
178	    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
179	    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
180	    refine Or.inr fun Q hQ => ?_
181	    have hQP : Q ≠ P := fun h => hP (h ▸ hQ)
182	    rw [← add_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne E hQP]
183	    exact ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx) Q hQ
184	  · exact sectionSub_mono k U (le_add_pointDivisor E P)
185	
186	/-- **The off-overlap χ-jump is exactly the ONE surviving chart step** — unconditionally.

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.ChiUnconditional
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.ResidueField

/-!
# Extension uniformity, reduced to a chart count uniform in the extension

`ResidueField.UniformlyBoundedVanishing` writes down cluster P's gap (2) — a **single**
vanishing threshold `b`, chosen before the field extension `κ/k` — and proves it at no
curve.  The two inputs its docstring records as genuinely missing are flat base change for
the section spaces and a `WeilDivisor` pullback along `C_κ ⟶ C`.

This file does **not** supply either.  What it does is remove the *cohomological* half of the
obstruction, using the ungated Čech formula of `ChiUnconditional.lean`:

`h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts` says `Ȟ¹(D) = 0` iff the three chart dimensions satisfy a
numerical identity.  That criterion mentions **no** connecting homomorphism, no exactness
datum, and nothing about `κ` beyond the chart dimensions themselves.  So extension
uniformity follows from a chart count that is uniform in `κ` — and the residual gap becomes a
statement about **dimensions of section spaces under base change**, which is exactly the flat
base change already identified as missing, and nothing more.

That is the honest gain: the gap does not shrink logically, but it stops being three
different things (vanishing + exactness + base change) and becomes one (base change).

## The three gaps, kept apart as the task requires

* **Single-field vanishing** — `ChiUnconditional.h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts` is an ungated
  *criterion*; whether its right-hand side holds at a given curve is not proved here or
  anywhere in AJC.  Still open, now purely a counting question.
* **Extension uniformity** — `uniformlyBoundedVanishing_of_uniformChartCount` below reduces
  it to `UniformChartCount`, a κ-uniform chart identity.  `UniformChartCount` is **not
  proved at any curve**; it is a hypothesis, and it is strictly stronger than the
  single-field count. Still open.
* **Global generation** — untouched here; see `GlobalGeneration.lean`.  It is proved from
  the ledger inputs and is *not* implied by anything in this file.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
open scoped WithZero AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

namespace AlgebraicGeometry
namespace Adelic

section UniformCharts

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- **The κ-uniform chart count.**  A single threshold `b`, chosen before the extension `κ`,
above which the Čech inclusion–exclusion count computes `ℓ` on the base-changed curve.

This is the base-change-side hypothesis, isolated.  Compare
`ChiUnconditional.h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts`, whose right-hand side is this identity at one
fixed field: `UniformChartCount` is that identity with `b` pulled outside the `∀ κ`, which is
precisely the uniformity the predicate `UniformlyBoundedVanishing` demands.

It is stated with the finiteness of the three base-changed chart section spaces as explicit
hypotheses in the body rather than as instance binders, because on the base-changed curve
those instances are exactly what a base-change theorem would produce, and demanding them as
binders here would quietly assume the missing input. -/
def UniformChartCount (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK κ D →
      sectionSub κ ((S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂) D ≤
        coboundarySub κ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ D

/-- **Extension-uniform vanishing from the κ-uniform chart count.**

The threshold transfers verbatim: `UniformChartCount`'s `b` is `UniformlyBoundedVanishing`'s
`b`, and at each `κ` and `D` the conclusion is `BoundedVanishing.subsingleton_h1Mod_iff`
applied to the chart inclusion.  No exactness hypothesis, no approximation input, no ledger.

**What this is and is not.**  It is a genuine reduction of *cluster P's gap (2)* to a
statement about base-changed section spaces — the cohomological content is discharged.  It is
**not** a proof of extension uniformity: `UniformChartCount` is unproved at every curve, and
it is strictly stronger than the single-field count because `b` is quantified before `κ`.
Anyone reading this as "extension uniformity is closed" has misread it; a janitor made
exactly that conflation once already (retracted at inbox `I-0412`). -/
theorem uniformlyBoundedVanishing_of_uniformChartCount
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (hcount : UniformChartCount C S) :
    UniformlyBoundedVanishing C S := by
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hcount
  refine ⟨b, fun κ _ _ D hD => ?_⟩
  exact (subsingleton_h1Mod_iff κ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ D).mpr
    (hb κ D hD)

end UniformCharts

end Adelic
end AlgebraicGeometry

section Sections

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]

/-- **N3 — the Riemann–Roch section subgroup `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`.** For an open
`U ⊆ X` and a Weil divisor `D`, the set of rational functions `f ∈ K(X)` whose
order along every prime divisor `P` meeting `U` is at least `-D(P)`:
`Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D)) = { f : f = 0 ∨ ∀ P ∈ U, ord_P f ≥ -D(P) }`.

The `f = 0` disjunct encodes the convention `ord_P 0 = +∞` (the project's junk
convention gives `ord_P 0 = 0`, so the zero function must be admitted separately).
Closure under addition is the `order` ultrametric `order_add_ge_min`. -/
def sectionOfDivisor (U : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
    AddSubgroup X.functionField where
  carrier := { f | f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
    -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f }
  zero_mem' := Or.inl rfl
  add_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg
    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
    · simpa using hg
    rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hgne
    · simpa using hf
    rcases eq_or_ne (f + g) 0 with h0 | h0
    · exact Or.inl h0
    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
    have hcf := (hf.resolve_left hfne) P hP
    have hcg := (hg.resolve_left hgne) P hP
    calc -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
        ≤ min (Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) (Scheme.RationalMap.order P g) :=
          le_min hcf hcg

    intro f hf
    rcases hf with rfl | hf
    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
    · refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
      rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_neg]
      exact hf P hP
